scope: contemporary Khmer descriptive model; phonetic values are evidence-backed inventories and representative mappings, not a complete deterministic orthography-to-IPA table

orthographic_principles.statement: The same dependent vowel sign may have different phonetic realizations after first- and second-series consonants.
Vowel length is contrastive and is encoded by different vowel signs in many cases; practical Ukrainian output normally neutralizes length unless a dedicated research mode preserves it.
Vowel harmony can affect the apparent series of a following syllable in relevant lexical environments; exceptions exist.
Unstressed vowels may reduce, especially in bisyllabic words; this is a pronunciation-profile phenomenon rather than a universal spelling substitution.
U+17C6 NIKAHIT participates in vowel/coda patterns and cannot be mapped as a simple independent vowel.
U+17C7 REAHMUK represents /h/ as a coda and also affects the preceding nucleus; it is not a generic vowel letter.

coverage_policy: Do not infer an exact IPA value for every vowel sign from the sign name alone. The future full matrix must condition on series, syllable openness/coda, stress, harmony, lexical category and pronunciation profile.
